title: Fatima Config
description: Configuration for Fatima providers, generators, models, and formatters. Fatima uses fatima.json as its project configuration file.

$schema.description: Optional JSON Schema URL used by editors to provide validation and autocomplete.

generator.description: Generator used to produce typed environment access files. Built-ins are language-agnostic targets: TypeScript, JavaScript, and Python. Plugins may register additional generators.

file.description: Output file path for generated typed environment access. Defaults depend on the selected generator, such as env.ts, env.js, or env.py.

formatter.description: Optional command used to format generated files. Use $1 as the generated file path placeholder.

environment.description: Expression used to resolve the active logical environment. Supports {env:NAME} interpolation, for example {env:NODE_ENV} ?? 'development'.

plugins.description: Plugin module specifiers or relative paths. Plugins can add providers, generators, and models.

publicPrefix.description: Prefix used to split public/client-safe variables from private variables in generators that support public outputs.

providers.description: Environment-specific provider chains. Each key is a logical environment and each value is the ordered list of providers used to load variables for that environment.

model.description: Runtime parsing and typing model for environment variables. Models validate, parse, and inform generator output.

providers.description: Provider chains keyed by logical environment name, such as development, staging, production, or preview.

additionalProperties.description: Ordered provider chain. Later providers can override or use values loaded by previous providers through {env:NAME} interpolation.

localProvider.description: Loads variables from one or more local .env files. The source files are not managed or encrypted by Fatima.

file.description: A single .env file or list of .env files to read.

files.description: List of .env files to read. Equivalent to passing an array through file.

fatimaLocalVaultProvider.description: Loads variables from the local encrypted Fatima vault.

provider.description: Use the built-in local encrypted Fatima vault provider.

auth.description: Authentication mode. Defaults to key when key is provided, otherwise password.

environment.description: Vault environment to read. Defaults to the active Fatima environment.

config.description: Optional fatima.json path used to locate .fatima.

cwd.description: Optional working directory used to resolve config or storePath.

storePath.description: Optional direct path to a .fatima store directory.

infisicalProvider.description: Loads variables from Infisical using the optional Infisical SDK.

clientId.description: Infisical machine identity client ID. Supports {env:NAME} interpolation.

clientSecret.description: Infisical machine identity client secret. Supports {env:NAME} interpolation.

siteUrl.description: Optional Infisical site URL for self-hosted instances.

herokuProvider.description: Loads config vars from a Heroku app.

environment.description: Logical or remote environment label. Supports {env:NAME} interpolation.

app_id_or_name.description: Heroku app ID or app name.

bearer_token.description: Heroku API bearer token. Supports {env:NAME} interpolation.

vercelProvider.description: Loads environment variables from a Vercel project.

environment.description: Vercel environment name, such as development, preview, or production.

pluginProvider.description: Provider supplied by a plugin. Additional plugin-specific properties are allowed.

models.description: Model map keyed by variable name. Models define runtime parsing behavior and generated typing.

builtinModelObject.description: Built-in model with model-specific arguments. Use args.values to restrict the parsed value to a finite set.

args.description: Arguments for the selected model. Editors autocomplete these based on the model type.

pluginModel.description: Model supplied by a plugin. Additional plugin-specific properties are allowed.
